lines: Morgan Patel
+1 (555) 010-4410 | morgan.patel@example.com | example.com/code/mpatel
EDUCATION
Ridgeway University | Ph.D. candidate in Statistics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2021 - Expected May 2026
Ridgeway University | B.S. in Mathematics | Metro City, USA | Sep 2016 - May 2020
EXPERIENCE
Sunrise Bakery | Assistant Store Manager | Metro City, USA | Sep 2025 - Present
- Managed opening shifts and a team of 6 bakers and cashiers, keeping the store within its weekly labour budget.
- Ran daily stock counts and supplier orders, cutting unsold bread from 12% to 7% of production.
Northpeak Capital | Quantitative Research Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2025 - Aug 2025
- Improved risk-adjusted returns by 35% with a cost-aware position smoother on the desk's futures signal.
- Validated the signal on 6 years of tick data with purged walk-forward splits and an embargo period, so every backtest decision used only information available at the time.
- Wrote a feature store for 120 microstructure features with point-in-time joins, which the research team reused in two later signal projects.
- Presented the signal, its capacity estimate and failure cases to the portfolio managers, who approved a small live allocation for the next quarter.
- Selected the smoother's parameters from 400 backtested configurations and reported the best one's Sharpe as the expected live Sharpe.
- Built a short-horizon order-book imbalance signal for liquid index futures that raised the desk book's Sharpe ratio from 1.1 to 1.5 over 18 months of out-of-sample backtest after costs.
Ridgeway University | Research Assistant, Statistical Learning Lab | Metro City, USA | Jun 2020 - Aug 2021
- Cut a 2,000-run Monte Carlo study from 3 days to 5 hours by running the runs in parallel with the same random seed on every worker.
- Derived a variance bound for a sparse regression estimator; my proof tightens the previous bound by a log factor and is now Section 3 of a paper under review at JASA.
- Taught weekly recitations for 60 students in graduate probability, writing 12 problem sets and earning a 4.8/5 teaching rating.
- Released an open-source R package for high-dimensional covariance estimation with shrinkage and factor models, downloaded 3,000 times in its first year.
PROJECTS
Volatility Forecasting Study | Independent Research | Python, PyTorch | Jan 2024 - Present
- Beat a HAR-RV baseline's out-of-sample QLIKE loss by 7% on 30 equity indices with a temporal convolutional model trained on realized-volatility features.
- Tested significance with Diebold-Mariano tests across the 30 indices; after a Holm correction the forecast gain held at the 5% level on 24 of them and in both crisis periods.
- Wrote up the method, robustness checks and results as a 12-page working paper, which was presented at the department's financial econometrics seminar.
Kaggle Market Prediction Competition | Team of 3 | Python | Mar 2023 - Jun 2023
- Engineered features and trained gradient-boosting models for a market prediction competition.
- Cut validation leakage by switching to time-grouped folds, which closed a 0.02 gap between local validation and leaderboard scores.
- Added 0.4 to the Sharpe ratio of a futures book with an order-book imbalance signal, tested over 18 months out of sample.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, R, PyTorch, Kafka
Methods: time-series econometircs, high-dimensional statistics, gradient boosting

items.says: Add a concise target-oriented summary.
items.because: A recruiter currently has to infer whether the target is quantitative research, quantitative development, statistical modeling, or academia.

items.says: Reorder the sections to prioritize Northpeak and the volatility project.
items.because: Quantitative research is present but not prioritized structurally.

items.says: Make Northpeak and the volatility project visually dominant over bakery management and teaching.
items.because: They are the strongest evidence for the target roles.

items.says: Verify that the code link leads to a real, polished portfolio.
items.because: An empty or generic repository can hurt more than having no link.

items.says: Add a location or work-authorization signal if relevant.
items.because: Finance employers may recruit by office or require specific authorization.

items.says: Consider adding a LinkedIn profile if it is complete and consistent.
items.because: An incomplete profile creates an avoidable credibility issue.

items.says: Add the Ph.D. research area or dissertation topic.
items.because: “Ph.D. candidate in Statistics” is broad for quantitative research readers.

items.says: Make candidacy status and availability unambiguous.
items.because: The expected date alone may not establish whether the degree will be completed before the target role begins.

items.says: Consider adding a few highly relevant courses.
items.because: They could strengthen the signal for the target role.

items.says: Consider adding an advisor, dissertation title, or research group when meaningful.
items.because: Those details can help for research-heavy quant positions.

items.says: Reduce the B.S. degree’s visual emphasis or remove it if space is needed.
items.because: Graduate training is more important, and the undergraduate degree is no longer essential near Ph.D. completion.

items.says: Move Sunrise below the quantitative experience or into Additional Experience.
items.because: Its current position may make store management look like the intended professional direction.

items.says: Present Sunrise as operational leadership rather than a central technical credential.
items.because: Its value is responsibility and execution, not quantitative finance expertise.

items.says: Clarify the scale, ownership, and result of the management work.
items.because: The bullet combines shift management, supervision, and budget control without showing the degree of responsibility or outcome.

items.says: Quantify the labor budget or an operational improvement if possible.
items.because: Staying within budget is a baseline expectation without a budget size, savings, or improvement.

items.says: Clarify whether the six employees were directly supervised or their work was coordinated.
items.because: The distinction matters for leadership credibility.

items.says: Explain what change reduced unsold bread.
items.because: Counts and orders do not show whether the improvement came from forecasting, timing, production adjustments, or supplier coordination.

items.says: Do not frame the reduction as a forecasting model unless one was built.
items.because: The evidence shown is a measurable operations improvement.

items.says: Name the metric behind “risk-adjusted returns.”
items.because: A technical reader cannot tell whether the 35% refers to Sharpe, information ratio, or another measure.

items.says: Give the comparison period, universe, transaction-cost assumptions, and baseline.
items.because: Without them, the 35% figure is difficult to evaluate and may appear inflated.

items.says: Reconcile the 35% improvement with the later increase from 1.1 to 1.5 Sharpe.
items.because: The figures may be consistent, but their relationship is not obvious.

items.says: Identify the individual contribution to the smoother.
items.because: “Improved” can imply ownership of the desk’s entire strategy.

items.says: Specify whether the validation covered the smoother, signal, full strategy, or pipeline.
items.because: The object being validated is unclear.

items.says: Clarify the embargo interval and its purpose if material.
items.because: A quant interviewer may ask what was embargoed and why.

items.says: Do not imply that leakage-resistant backtesting proves live performance.
items.because: It supports the backtest’s credibility but does not establish that the strategy will work live.

items.says: Describe the feature store’s implementation and engineering scope.
items.because: A reviewer cannot tell what work covered versioning, storage, latency, testing, or deployment.

items.says: Clarify what the two later projects reused.
items.because: It could have been the infrastructure, the features, or both.

items.says: Clarify the role in the live-allocation decision.
items.because: Approval by portfolio managers should not imply that the intern managed capital or made the final decision.

items.says: Add the allocation’s scale or risk limits if permitted.
items.because: A “small live allocation” is otherwise difficult to interpret.

items.says: Identify the failure cases presented.
items.because: The current wording leaves the failure-mode analysis underdeveloped.

items.says: Reporting the best of 400 configurations’ Sharpe as expected live Sharpe is not defensible as written.
items.because: Selecting the best trial creates a multiple-testing and selection-bias problem without independent evaluation.

items.says: The order-book imbalance signal and performance result appear duplicated in the Kaggle project.
items.because: The repetition creates uncertainty about where the work was done and whether the result is being double-counted.

items.says: Explain what “the desk book” refers to.
items.because: It could mean an existing portfolio, a simulated book, or a research portfolio.

items.says: Substantiate the 18-month out-of-sample test and its constraints.
items.because: It is unclear whether the period was untouched during selection or accounted for slippage, capacity, and changing regimes.

items.says: Add constraints or diagnostics rather than relying on the Sharpe increase alone.
items.because: A Sharpe increase by itself does not establish production readiness.

items.says: Using the same random seed on every worker may produce duplicate or correlated simulation streams.
items.because: That would undermine the Monte Carlo study.

items.says: Add the parallel-computing implementation environment if relevant.
items.because: Cluster execution, vectorization, or job scheduling could be useful quant-research signals.

items.says: Make the proof’s ownership and manuscript authorship precise.
items.because: “My proof” and “Section 3” may overstate the individual role.

items.says: State the manuscript’s exact review or publication status consistently.
items.because: Under review, accepted, and published have materially different credibility.

items.says: Avoid overstating the proof’s connection to finance.
items.because: Its value is statistical theory, proof ability, and technical rigor.

items.says: Move the teaching bullet below the research and software bullets.
items.because: Teaching is not among the strongest quant credentials.

items.says: Give the source and scale of the teaching rating if retaining it.
items.because: The 4.8/5 rating should be legitimate and not outweigh research results.

items.says: Clarify whether the course material was designed or only delivered.
items.because: That determines the level of ownership.

items.says: Move the package bullet ahead of teaching.
items.because: It demonstrates software development, public delivery, and adoption.

items.says: State how the 3,000 downloads were measured.
items.because: CRAN, GitHub, and other sources carry different meanings.

items.says: Add available evidence of package quality.
items.because: Tests, documentation, continuous integration, or outside use would strengthen the claim.

items.says: Name or link the package if it is publicly available and polished.
items.because: A reviewer could then substantiate the technical claim.

items.says: Give the data period and forecast horizon.
items.because: Both materially affect interpretation of the 7% result.

items.says: Explain the out-of-sample design and hyperparameter selection.
items.because: The current wording does not establish that the baseline comparison is fair.

items.says: Show why a temporal convolutional model was appropriate if space allows.
items.because: The methodological reasoning is not apparent from the result alone.

items.says: Clarify the unit of the 5% significance result.
items.because: It is unclear whether tests were separate for each index, across horizons, or structured another way.

items.says: Say whether the crisis periods were pre-specified.
items.because: Selection after examining the data would affect the robustness claim’s credibility.

items.says: Keep the test detail from overwhelming the forecasting result.
items.because: The bullet should support the practical claim rather than read like a methods appendix.

items.says: Make clear that the working paper is not a publication.
items.because: Its status should not be mistaken for a published paper.

items.says: Link the paper or presentation if available.
items.because: A technical reviewer may want to inspect the methodology.

items.says: State whether the paper was sole-authored or team work.
items.because: Authorship matters when evaluating ownership.

items.says: Add the competition result or remove the bullet.
items.because: It lists activities without performance, ranking, or a concrete technical outcome.

items.says: Specify the dataset or prediction task if it establishes relevance.
items.because: Generic competition language does not differentiate the work.

items.says: Explain the leakage mechanism and resulting validation design.
items.because: That would substantiate the claimed understanding of temporal validation.

items.says: Explain what improvement closing the 0.02 gap represents.
items.because: A smaller validation-leaderboard gap is not automatically positive without knowing whether overestimation fell or leaderboard performance improved.

items.says: Distinguish this work from Northpeak if they are connected.
items.because: Competition and professional work should not be presented as independent evidence when they are not.

items.says: The order-book imbalance signal and 18-month Sharpe result appear duplicated at Northpeak.
items.because: Repeating the same concept and period looks padded and may double-count the result.

items.says: If this was separate work, distinguish its dataset, signal, period, and portfolio construction.
items.because: Otherwise its difference from the Northpeak result is unclear.

items.says: Use terminology that reflects the competition environment.
items.because: “Futures book” could imply ownership of a real book if it was only a simulated competition portfolio.

items.says: Add specific research, data, testing, and infrastructure tools used in the work.
items.because: The skills list is thin and does not show enough of the research or production-quality workflow.

items.says: Support or remove Kafka.
items.because: It appears without evidence of meaningful use and can look like keyword stuffing.

items.says: Separate research languages from production or infrastructure tools.
items.because: That would make the technical profile clearer.

items.says: “Econometircs” is misspelled.
items.because: A spelling error in a core target-domain skill is especially damaging.

items.says: Use consistent, conventional method names.
items.because: The terminology should align with the projects and publications.

items.says: Add methods demonstrated by the résumé.
items.because: The work shows validation, forecasting, simulation, inference, and other methods absent from the list.
